findings: Controller: direct site correction without extra experience reaches4/6, mean.2333333333333333. Add one actual keep observation and it reaches5/6, mean.5466666666666666, exactly matching all v144 TwoStepValue main traces and post-experience R+L/I.

Plant: own controller entry is absent; direct policy keeps without trying deletion. Both direct versions remain0/6, mean-1.02. PlusExperience still matches old TwoStepValue main raw/state exactly; no claim to fix the plant.

Matched PlusExperience uses only two real private tasks for the two cases instead of eight; same first keep trace is consumed exactly once per case, no private L copy and no NoWrite ordinary-learning freeze.

TwoStepValue is not necessary to obtain the recorded benefit in these cases. Mechanism correction and one real ordinary experience explain it; a simpler explicit own-state policy supplies the selection.

The initial task-visible evidence across mechanisms was identical, but the complete learner-owned X state was not: one case has the site override, the other does not. Reading this available own state distinguishes them without paid candidate tests, not by leaking evaluator truth.
limits: New direct baseline is an explicitly unvalidated local heuristic: a present nonidentity controller mapping is not universally wrong. Do not globally adopt deletion without testing desired/compensating mappings and alternative causal mechanisms.

Own-controller access is a richer policy input than the old evidence-only candidate generator exploited, although the same own state was physically available to all learners. This is not a proof that no learning or experiment can add value on harder inputs.
One ordinary patch checkpoint, two informed fixed cases, manualMAX stream; not blind independent seeds, architecture ranking, general causal inference or formal science confirmation.
